_about: Where the original reads differently from the Berean at a word that matters, shown at the word itself: an asterisk in the verse and the finding beside it, marked as the site's own. The Berean's words are never changed. Doug, 2026-10-08: 'keep Berean's words - but make the note clearly marked - even with an asterisk or equivalent right in the verse - this is for consistency in using a translation but communicating our findings.' Each finding: the verse (site id), the Berean's exact words to mark, the original word (lemma) and MACULA's gloss, and a note in plain words. Every finding is checked against MACULA (© Biblica) before it goes in; tests/test_translation_findings.py checks each 'word' is in its verse.

findings.note: The Greek verb here is παύω, which MACULA glosses "they will be ceased". It is a different verb from the one said of prophecies and knowledge in the same verse (καταργέω, "done away", "pass away").
The Hebrew word is בְּרִית (berit), the word for covenant: "he made a covenant with them to let them live".
The Hebrew verb is מוּג, which MACULA glosses "melted": "you have melted us in the hand of our iniquity" (64:6 in the Hebrew numbering).
The capital in "His" is the Berean's. The Greek reads "as the high priests, first for the own sins": the sins offered for first are the high priests'.
